Figure 26: ER diagram of the system 

10. # **Size and Performance**  {#size-and-performance}

**10.1 Size**   
The chunk size is configured at 100 rows per chunk and not in terms of number of chunks to ensure that the payload size and time of invocation don't vary irrespective of variation in size of the upload; 10,000 row upload becomes 100 chunks and not 200 rows as in the previous case. The Map State Concurrency is capped at 10 which will ensure that the number of concurrent RDS connections made by the Load Lambda (only stage with live database connection) remains below this number.

Memory Allocation to the Lambdas is done unevenly across 18 lambdas in deployment based on their genuine requirements and not on one uniform basis:

| Service Group | Lambda Name | Memory | Runs | Job |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Auth & User | auth-api | 256-512 MB | per request | Registration, login, profile CRUD |
| Marketplace | marketplace-api | 256-512 MB | per request | Listings CRUD, favourites |
| Marketplace | search-api | \~3008 MB | per query | NL parser, Groq fallback, MiniLM, pgvector |
| Ingestion | ingest-upload-api | 512 MB | per request | Upload intake, multi-part streams, S3/SQS |
| Ingestion | job-status-api | 256 MB | per request | High-frequency job status polling |
| Admin | admin-api | 256-512 MB | per request | Dashboards, user management, reports |
| Notification | notification-worker | 256 MB | per event | SES email dispatch |
| ETL Pipeline | validateFile function | 256 MB | once/upload | Headers, encoding, row count, ZIP integrity |
| ETL Pipeline | splitChunks function | 512 MB | once/upload | Rows \-\> chunk descriptors \-\> S3 |
| ETL Pipeline | parseNormalize function | 512 MB | per chunk | Parse \+ dictionaries \+ regex \+ confidence |
| ETL Pipeline | groqNormalize function | 256 MB | per flagged | LLM repair (own retry \+ Catch) |
| ETL Pipeline | validateRows function | 256 MB | per chunk | Mandatory fields \-\> rejected\_records |
| ETL Pipeline | enrich function | 512 MB | per chunk | Derivations, JSONB, search\_text |
| ETL Pipeline | embed function | \~3008 MB | per chunk | MiniLM \-\> 384-dim vector |
| ETL Pipeline | load function | 512 MB | per chunk | Bulk insert \-\> vehicles as PENDING\_REVIEW |
| ETL Pipeline | images function | \~2048 MB | once/upload | Sharp resize \+ row↔photo matching |
| ETL Pipeline | aggregate function | 256 MB | once/upload | Tally accepted/rejected/flagged |
| ETL Pipeline | notify function | 256 MB | once/upload | Trigger Notification Service |

For a representative 1,000-row upload at 100 rows/chunk, this design produces roughly 61 Lambda invocations across one Step Functions execution (versus 10 invocations for a single fused Lambda alternative), a deliberate trade of invocation count for per-stage retry granularity, memory-appropriate billing, and declarative failure handling.

**10.2 Performance targets**

 average API response under 500 ms for CRUD/browse endpoints, under 2 s for natural-language search; design capacity of up to 10,000 listings and 100 concurrent users at prototype scale; graceful fallback to filter/trigram search if semantic ranking degrades.

11. # **Quality**  {#quality}

**11.1 Reliability**

Step Functions' declarative Retry/Catch on the Groq step means an LLM outage degrades a 1,000-row upload to roughly 95% success (rules-only) instead of failing the entire upload

Row-level idempotent persistence and a dead-letter queue prevent duplicate or silently-lost records on reprocessing.

**11.2 Security**

JWT-based stateless authentication with revocable, hashed refresh tokens; role-based guards at the controller level

Least-privilege IAM per Lambda function, notably that groqNormalize function resolves make/model against an in-memory table snapshot rather than holding a live database connection, keeping the RDS connection-pool argument intact.

**11.3 Scalability**

The Map state's per-chunk fan-out and Lambda's automatic scaling mean upload throughput scales with chunk count rather than a fixed worker pool

Fixing rows-per-chunk (not chunk count) keeps this scaling well-behaved as upload size grows.

**11.4 Maintainability** 

The shared normalize+embed library is the single mechanism preventing vocabulary and model drift between the ingestion and search halves of the system

Per-service schema ownership within one physical database keeps logical boundaries clear without the operational cost of five separate RDS instances.

**11.5 Extensibility** 

JSONB per-vehicle-type attributes mean new vehicle types (beyond car/bike/van/truck) require no schema migration

Unmapped CSV columns are preserved as searchable "extras" rather than discarded, so dealer-specific data is never silently lost.

**11.6 Observability** 

Every ETL stage's status, retry count, and error message is logged to etl\_stage\_logs from the first version

Step Functions provides a live, per-execution graph in the AWS console without any custom tooling

Every provenance-tagged field (source: RULES vs GROQ, with confidence) is retained through to the dealer review UI.
